title: Lifecycle events carry only allowed metadata fields and drop forbidden keys
asA: reviewer verifying the platform-cloudflare-durable-objects v1.0.0 blueprint at mechanism reach
iWant: the event-secrecy probe to drive namespaceReady, doAccept, doAlarmFired, doWakeUp and doHibernate through the shipped code path and assert no record carries any forbidden key (body, ssn, userId, headers, cookies)
soThat: a logging companion can render the sink directly without a per-blueprint scrub pass

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every record emitted on the sink by createDoFacade, SingleCellObject.alarm() and HubObject.accept/hibernate/wake is a plain object whose top-level keys are drawn from the allowed set {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp, objectName, scheduledTime}. No record carries body, ssn, userId, headers, cookies, request or payload; the probe returns aggregateVerdict: pass with a zero-hit count on the forbidden-key scan. Under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true a wrapped sink forwards a synthetic body-bearing record and the probe surfaces the forbidden keys, returning aggregateVerdict: fail.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a driven facade + single-cell + hub with an accumulating spy sink
acceptanceCriteria.when: the event-secrecy probe runs on the shipped code path
acceptanceCriteria.then: every record contains only allowed keys; the forbidden-key scan finds zero hits; SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true surfaces the injected fields

acceptanceCriteria.description: Allow-list mutation: a wrapper sink that adds a top-level "requestId" key onto every record trips the layer-1 forbidden-key scan (requestId is not in the allow-list). The event-secrecy probe surfaces the key by name and returns aggregateVerdict:"fail". Under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=false (the shipped path) no wrapper is in play and the scan returns zero forbidden hits.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the event-secrecy probe under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true with a wrapper adding "requestId" onto every record
acceptanceCriteria.when: the layer-1 scan runs on the accumulated records
acceptanceCriteria.then: the scan surfaces "requestId" as a forbidden key; aggregateVerdict is "fail"

acceptanceCriteria.description: Closure-over-fixture: a hub handler that captures a PII fixture ({userId:12345, ssn:"REDACTED-fixture"}) via a JavaScript closure and mutates a scratch object each call still produces sink records whose JSON serialisation contains no "12345" and no "REDACTED-fixture" substring. Layer-2 substring scan returns zero hits on the shipped path (SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=false).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a hub handler closing over a PII fixture on the shipped path
acceptanceCriteria.when: the event-secrecy probe runs a broadcast that triggers the handler
acceptanceCriteria.then: the layer-2 substring scan on the emitted records returns zero hits for the PII substrings

acceptanceCriteria.description: Empty-payload boundary: a broadcast with an empty body ({type:"broadcast", payload:""}) still emits doBroadcast records on the sink carrying the required allow-list keys (event, key, size:0, ttl:null, timestamp:<number>, objectName:<hub id>). No allow-list key is silently omitted when the payload is empty; size reports 0 rather than undefined.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a HubObject broadcasting an empty payload
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sink is inspected after the broadcast
acceptanceCriteria.then: the doBroadcast record carries every required allow-list key with size:0 (never undefined)
